Can you confirm the network connectivity pattern you prefer for a live co-sell demo? Specifically: 

- Do you want classic VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink endpoints, or a combination?
- Required CIDR ranges and expected ACL rules (ingress/egress)
- IAM/service account requirements for the demo instances
- Any timing constraints for AWS account invitations / resource sharing (IAM/ORG/RAM)

We have a test AWS account ready (acct: 987654321) and can carve a /24 for the demo VPC. If you have a short checklist or diagram you can share that would be ideal. Also looping in Vivek for any SRE constraints.

Best,

Subject: Re: Joint demo: network access + VPC peering checklist

Hi Alice —

Thanks — attached is a lightweight checklist we use for marketplace demos (vpc-peering-checklist.pdf). TL;DR recommendation for this demo: prefer PrivateLink for the control-plane API endpoints and VPC peering for high-throughput telemetry if you need sub-100ms p99s for agent callbacks. That combo gives a good security posture while avoiding broad route table exposure.

Quick summary from the checklist: 
- Control plane: AWS PrivateLink (NLB + interface endpoints) — requires owner to create interface endpoint, share AZ subnet IDs.
- Data plane: VPC peering (one-way routes) if you need bulk token flows; otherwise use S3/managed endpoints for artifact exchange.
- Required ports: TCP 443 (API), TCP 22 (if SSH jump needed — please avoid for demo), ephemeral high ports only if demo VM initiates reverse connections.
- IAM: create a read-only service role for the demo with sts:AssumeRole; we'll provide a sample policy.
- Timing: PrivateLink endpoints and peering can be completed within 2 business days if account invites are accepted promptly.

Attached: vpc-peering-checklist.pdf (stub).

Next steps: Ben, can you confirm the demo network diagram and whether we should request Privatelink only (to avoid peering) vs. peering+Privatelink? Alice — if you can confirm your AWS account contact and preferred demo date (we suggested Oct 27), we'll start provisioning.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachments: vpc-peering-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Joint demo: network access + VPC peering checklist

Connor / Alice —

Appended a quick diagram (demo-network-diagram.png) showing the two recommended topologies: 1) Privatelink-only (control + data via interface endpoints + S3 for artifacts) and 2) Hybrid (Privatelink for control, VPC peering for high-throughput telemetry). Notes: 

- If NimbleOps prefers not to open routes, Privatelink-only is the least operationally risky and often works fine for a 20–30 minute demo.
- For the hybrid path we'll need route table entries in both VPCs and a brief security group rule to allow 10.0.0.0/24 <-> 172.31.32.0/24.
- Cross-account IAM: create a role named demo/RedwoodAssumeRole with this policy (see inline sample in the checklist).
- Privatelink caveat: requires subnets in at least two AZs for endpoint resilience; please confirm which AZs you can open.

I've attached demo-network-diagram.png (stub) and a 1-page ops note (privatelink-ops-notes.txt) with the commands we use.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Partner Technical Lead, Redwood Inference

That said, if you can demonstrate the hybrid path in an isolated test account that's fine.

Can you also confirm how long the PrivateLink endpoint provisioning takes from your side and whether the HubSpot record HS-78321 needs any additional documentation before co-sell approval?

- Provisioning timeline: once Alice confirms the target subnets (AZs) we can request interface endpoints from our side; expect ~24–48 hours for endpoint creation and validation if security groups are ready.
- Documentation: I uploaded the checklist + diagram to Drive and filed an update on HS-78321. Links below.
- Demo date: tentatively Oct 27, 10:00am PT — Alice, please confirm and we'll send calendar invites + pre-demo runbook.
